parole.testo: Borrowed from French abordage, from French aborder + -age (< Latin -āticum). Further from French a- (< Latin ad-) + French bord (< Proto-Germanic *burdą, whence also English board; Dutch boord, German Bord, whence Russian борт (bort)) + French -er (< Latin -āre).
From French bande. Further from Proto-Germanic [Term?]. Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰendʰ-. Compare typologically сою́з (sojúz) (akin to вяза́ть (vjazátʹ), свя́зка (svjázka), у́зы (úzy)).
Borrowed from French garage. Omitting several steps, from Proto-Germanic *warōną. Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *wer- (whence also Latin vereor).
Borrowed from French guirlande, further from or related to Proto-Germanic *wīraz (whence English wire). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *weh₁y-.
Borrowed from French croupe. Omitting several steps, from Proto-Germanic *kruppaz. Doublet of гру́ппа (grúppa) and крупье́ (krupʹjé).

parole.significato: croupier (person who collects bets and pays out winnings at a gambling table)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French croupier. Omitting several steps, from Proto-Germanic *kruppaz + the suffix derived from Latin -ārius. Doublet of гру́ппа (grúppa) and круп (krup).
Borrowed from French fourrage, from Old French fourage, from Old French fuerre + -age. Further from Proto-Germanic *fōdrą + Latin -āticum. Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂-.
